units.name: Supply Chain and Systems Intelligence
units.evidence: Official page calls this a department, names its chair, and explicitly covers Operations & Supply Chain Management alongside IS, analytics and AI.

units.name: Department of Mechanical Engineering
units.evidence: Official department home names department and college, Mechanical Engineering PhD and manufacturing systems concentration. Linked graduate programme doctoral and manufacturing specialization sections explicitly cover production integration, cellular manufacturing, ergonomics, reliability/quality and complex manufacturing systems; this is substantive IE/Operations scope within the actual Mechanical host, not an invented Industrial Engineering department.

decisions.reason: Imported operations/supply-chain acronym is represented by full current combined department name.

sources.note: Full department name, chair and operations/supply-chain remit.

2026-27 engineering inventory lists biomedical, civil/construction/environmental, electrical/computer and mechanical engineering. Applied Supply Chain, Engineering & Technology is a concentration, not another department.

Mechanical doctoral and Manufacturing and Materials Systems Engineering accordions expanded and read. Doctoral outcomes explicitly require one of three departmental specializations and original research; manufacturing specialization explicitly includes cellular manufacturing, production integration, ergonomics, reliability/quality, human performance/safety, complex manufacturing systems and quality systems. This substantive production-system/ergonomics scope supports IE/Operations classification; materials processes alone would not.

Official department home explicitly names Department of Mechanical Engineering, Opus College of Engineering, and Doctor of Philosophy in Mechanical Engineering with manufacturing systems concentration.

Biomedical MS/PhD full specialization inventory read: bioinstrumentation, biomechanics, imaging, cellular/molecular, computational biology/bioinformatics and rehabilitation. No separate Operations specialization established.

Electrical/Computer PhD detail and all nested specialization accordions read. Electrical: signal processing, communications, controls, power/energy, devices/microsystems; Computer: ML/algorithms, embedded/IoT, vision/image processing. No explicit qualifying Operations specialization; methods alone not classified as OR.

limitations: No standalone Industrial Engineering department inferred; qualifying manufacturing/ergonomics scope is hosted in Mechanical Engineering.
